verses.verse:
शतम् शतम् समाहन्या दंगुलीयान् पृथक् पृथक्।
अंग पीड़ाम् प्रसहयैव ह्यंग शक्तिः प्रवर्धते।८१।
verses.text: One should strike the fingers a hundred times each, one by one; by enduring pain in the limb, the strength of the limb grows.

commentary.text: In this age of short lives, a special kind of practice for quick success is described in this śloka. Once the placement of the fingers on the flute is well established, each finger should be struck in its place, separately, a hundred times each, so that with unbroken practice pain begins in the finger; and by keeping even the aching finger moving, strength will come quickly to the fingers, just as heating iron quickly makes it pliable. At the same time the mind, busy with counting, also gains concentration. If the fingers of both hands are struck one at a time, by turns, progress can be even faster. In the same way, it will be fitting first to cook the breath, the tongue and the fingers separately for a while, as described above — like rice, dal and vegetables — in the fire of practice with the water of faith added, and then to combine all three and move on to the practice of svara (notes) and laya (tempo). On this, see the śloka —

subsection.title: Practice of the Tongue and of the Fingers
